statement: If one mean proportional number fall between two numbers, the numbers will be similar plane numbers.
heath_proof: For let one mean proportional number C fall between the two numbers A, B;I say that A, B are similar plane numbers. Let D, E, the least numbers of those which have the same ratio with A, C, be taken; [VII. 33] therefore D measures A the same number of times that E measures C. [VII. 20] Now, as many times as D measures A, so many units let there be in F; therefore F by multiplying D has made A, so that A is plane, and D, F are its sides. Again, since D, E are the least of the numbers which havethe same ratio with C, B, therefore D measures C the same number of times that E measures B. [VII. 20] As many times, then, as E measures B, so many units let there be in G;therefore E measures B according to the units in G; therefore G by multiplying E has made B. Therefore B is plane, and E, G are its sides. Therefore A, B are plane numbers. I say next that they are also similar. For, since F by multiplying D has made A, and by multiplying E has made C, therefore, as D is to E, so is A to C, that is, C to B. [VII. 17] Again, since E by multiplying F, G has made C, B respectively,therefore, as F is to G, so is C to B. [VII. 17] But, as C is to B, so is D to E; therefore also, as D is to E, so is F to G. And alternately, as D is to F, so is E to G. [VII. 13] Therefore A, B are similar plane numbers; for their sidesare proportional.

**Statement:** If one mean proportional number fall between two numbers, the numbers will be similar plane numbers.

**Step 1.** Let M be a mean proportional number between A and C. Thus A:M = M:C. We must show that A and C are plane numbers with proportional sides. [Hypothesis; D7.20; D7.21]

**Step 2.** Take p and q to be the least terms having the ratio A:M. Then p:q = A:M = M:C. We choose this route because least terms provide factors of both extremes directly. [7.33]

**Step 3.** Since the least terms measure corresponding terms of every pair having their ratio the same number of times, let p measure A and q measure M each r times; likewise, let p measure M and q measure C each s times. Hence
A = pr,  M = qr,  M = ps,  C = qs.
[7.20; D7.15]

**Step 4.** The two expressions for M give qr = ps. Consequently p:q = r:s, since the product of the extremes equals the product of the means. This equal-products criterion is the direct route from the factorizations to the required proportion. [CN1; 7.19]

**Step 5.** Since A = pr and C = qs, A and C are plane numbers with sides p, r and q, s respectively. Their corresponding sides are proportional, since p:q = r:s. Therefore A and C are similar plane numbers, as required. [D7.16; D7.21]
